newsitem.title: FRANCE: French SNCF rail plan eyes 2 bln FFR deficit in 97.
newsitem.headline: French SNCF rail plan eyes 2 bln FFR deficit in 97.

text.p: France's SNCF state railways said on Thursday that it had adopted a budget plan which envisaged narrowing its loss to two billion francs this year from a deficit of 15.2 billion francs in 1996.

It said it planned to achieve this target mainly by limiting fare increases in order to boost volumes, with a goal of keeping tariff increases to no more than 0.5 percent on average, which translated to a drop of one percent at constant prices.
"The SNCF has fixed costs on such a scale that it can only get back towards breakeven by regaining volumes," chairman Louis Gallois said.

The government is currently in the middle of reforming the railways' debt structure to take over 134 billion out of 208 billion francs in debts. The debt was incurred through building up the TGV high-speed rail network.
